fields.vectorRole: Mosquitoes (Culex, Culiseta or Aedes for bird species) take up gametocytes, host the sexual and sporogonic cycle, and inject sporozoites when feeding.
fields.distribution: Worldwide in birds; poultry outbreaks mostly in Africa, Asia and South America
fields.significance: Avian malaria: usually silent, but P. gallinaceum and P. durae can kill many commercial chickens or turkeys, and P. relictum threatens wild birds.

lifecycleStages.name: sporozoite
lifecycleStages.location: injected by a feeding mosquito

lifecycleStages.name: exoerythrocytic meront
lifecycleStages.location: endothelial cells of capillaries in brain, lung, liver and spleen of birds

lifecycleStages.name: erythrocytic meront
lifecycleStages.location: multiplies asexually inside red blood cells

lifecycleStages.name: gametocyte
lifecycleStages.location: red blood cells, taken up by a feeding mosquito

lifecycleStages.name: zygote and ookinete
lifecycleStages.location: mosquito midgut

lifecycleStages.name: oocyst
lifecycleStages.location: mosquito midgut wall; releases sporozoites that reach the salivary glands

fields.vectorRole: The brown dog tick is the definitive host; dogs are infected by swallowing an infected tick, not by its bite.
fields.distribution: Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas
fields.significance: Tick-borne infection of dogs and wild canids, usually mild or subclinical but sometimes causing fever, lethargy and anaemia.

lifecycleStages.name: oocyst
lifecycleStages.location: haemocoel of the tick

lifecycleStages.name: sporozoite
lifecycleStages.location: released in the dog gut after the tick is swallowed

lifecycleStages.name: meront
lifecycleStages.location: canine spleen, lymph nodes and bone marrow

lifecycleStages.name: gamont
lifecycleStages.location: inside circulating leucocytes, taken up by a feeding tick
